attempts.exactPrompt:
Create one original Summonlab candidate summon portrait as a cinematic semi-realistic painted drawing. Use visible brush planes and controlled illustrative detail: not a photograph, not photoreal skin, not plastic 3D, and not cel anime. Portrait canvas 1024 x 1536. Exactly one weaponless adult, full body, three-quarter standing pose, with the entire head, both hands, both feet, hair, clothing, and all accessories fully inside a generous safe margin. Warm pale parchment studio wash, restrained warm color response, soft grounding shadow, no environmental story.

New identity Lorin Pelleth: 22-year-old woman, 173 cm (medium), healthy slight, narrow, long-limbed construction with low mass, skin value band-3-light-medium. Face: angular diamond face; deep-set eyes and a heavy level brow; crooked healed nose, balanced mouth; one cheek mole. Calm closed-mouth neutral expression with no smile, grin, or theatrical acting.

Hair: red-copper-auburn, braids-twists-locs, deliberate accent: offset braid mass. Wardrobe: tailored-longcoat, specifically a cloth longcoat with a readable waist, split hem, plain underlayer, and fitted shoes; a high soft collar and uneven layered hems; bounded palette ochre-cream. Visible personal details: one small nape tattoo. Make a tattoo, scar, freckle field, or birthmark the primary recognition device. Maintenance cue: ornate hair maintenance with plain clothing care. Color treatment: uses small rhythmic repeats of the palette. Pose cue: chin remains level while one hand lightly checks a cuff seam. Include a small empty medicine pouch only as a quiet personal object, never as a weapon.

This is ordinary but intentionally designed 1-star mortal clothing. No weapon, armor, crown, magic, aura, or glow. No affinity cue, elemental gem, floating, frame, printed star, number, UI, logo, watermark, text, extra person, duplicated anatomy, cropped extremity, or published-character resemblance. Fantasy hair colors are matte dye or pigment, never supernatural emission. Preserve plausible anatomy while allowing the declared body construction to be extreme. Do not copy the reference's person, braid, clothes, pose, palette, progression, identity, body, hair, garments, ornaments, or markings.

RESERVE ACTIVATION: This is a fresh base summon, not an edit or regeneration of any existing hero. Create the new identity described above using only the authorized rendering-style reference. Honor the complete activated physical manifest and reserve character kernel; no failed hero or failed candidate is a visual source.

findings.observation: Original-resolution inspection shows exactly one adult woman with one coherent body and no duplicated anatomy.
The complete head and hair, both hands, both fitted shoes, longcoat hems, and medicine pouch remain wholly inside generous margins.
Visible brush planes across skin, copper hair, layered cloth, and parchment staging read as cinematic semi-realistic painting rather than photography, plastic 3D, or cel anime.

The slight long-limbed build, angular face, copper hair, ochre-cream split longcoat, high collar, uneven hems, fitted shoes, cuff-check pose, and medicine pouch are legible, but the required one small nape tattoo became a side-neck motif; added facial freckling, earrings, necklace, braid cuff, trouser ornaments, and dangling charms exceed density 1, while the single cheek mole and brow notch are not cleanly isolated.
The mouth is closed and unsmiling; chin, deep-set gaze, and heavy brow remain controlled without theatrical acting.
The figure remains an ordinary grounded mortal in cloth clothing with a small pouch and no weapon, armor, crown, magic, aura, affinity cue, glow, frame, star, number, UI, logo, watermark, or text.

The angular face and tailored coat differ, but the shaved-side, extremely long ringed braid draped over one shoulder reproduces the reference’s dominant hair silhouette and ornament construction too closely for the strict non-transfer gate.

attempts.retryReason: Strict inspection rejected manifest fidelity and original identity. The orchestrator authorized exactly one call and no correction, so no corrective attempt was made.
